42859062.label: Background
42859062.text: Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) received a Class 1 recommendation in the 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain guideline, yet the trajectory of Medicare payment for cardiac CT over the Category I era has not been systematically quantified.

42859062.label: Methods
42859062.text: January-effective Physician Fee Schedule Relative Value Files were compiled for 2010 through 2026 for CPT 75571-75574, with FFR-CT (75580) and AI-based plaque analysis (75577) from their Category I dates, and CT angiography of the chest (71275) as a non-cardiac comparator. National unadjusted non-facility payment (all geographic indices 1.000) was calculated for global, professional, and technical components as total relative value units (RVUs) multiplied by the conversion factor, adjusted to 2026 dollars using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), with the Medicare Economic Index (MEI) as a sensitivity analysis, and summarized as total real change and compound annual growth rate (CAGR). Claims volumes for 2013-2024 were obtained from CMS public use files, expressed per 1000 fee-for-service Part B enrollees, and the change in real allowed fee schedule spending was partitioned into unit revenue, volume, and interaction effects.

42859062.label: Results
42859062.text: Inflation-adjusted global payment declined for all four core codes between 2010 and 2026: -68.3% for CCTA (75574; CAGR -6.93%/y), -53.6% for congenital cardiac CT (75573), -50.2% for structural cardiac CT (75572), and -27.4% for coronary calcium scoring (75571). Declines concentrated in the technical component (-74.8% for 75574; RVU reductions of up to 58.7%), whereas professional payment fell 35.9%-37.5% with work RVUs unchanged until the 2.5% efficiency adjustment of 2026, attributable to a 38.8% real decline in the conversion factor. Results were unchanged under the MEI (-68.6% for CCTA) and modestly attenuated under the MEI net of productivity (-65.0%). Chest CT angiography fell 57.9%, with a professional decline close to the cardiac codes (-40.7%) but a smaller technical decline (-62.5% vs -74.8%). The largest single-year reduction occurred in 2011 (-36.4% for 75574). In the five years after the 2021 guideline, real global payment fell a further 24.2%-34.2%. Over 2013-2024, CCTA volume rose 408% while mean real allowed charge per service fell 45.9%, a decline that partly reflects migration of billing to facility settings. Real allowed fee schedule spending rose $22.0 million, comprising a $51.4 million volume effect offset by unit revenue (-$5.8 million) and interaction (-$23.6 million) effects; hospital technical payment is not captured.

42859062.label: Conclusion
42859062.text: Medicare payment for cardiac CT has declined steeply in real terms since Category I code adoption, and the decline accelerated during the period of strongest guideline endorsement. It exceeded the decline of a non-cardiac comparator and was insensitive to the choice of deflator. This discordance has implications for access, service-line viability, and payment policy advocacy. Aggregate fee schedule spending nonetheless rose over 2013-2024, driven entirely by volume growth rather than by valuation.

42859212.label: Purpose
42859212.text: To investigate the value of radiomics based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis (PPAP) after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD).

42859212.label: Methods
42859212.text: A retrospective analysis included 104 patients who underwent PD and preoperative CECT between May 2019 and March 2025. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 73) and test (n = 31) sets at a 7:3 ratio. PPAP was defined according to the biochemical and radiologic components of the International Study Group for Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) criteria. After pancreatic parenchyma delineation, radiomics feature extraction and selection, an optimal model was developed on the training set to calculate the radiomics score (rad-score). Independent clinical and morphological features were selected by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Conventional quantitative CT attenuation ratios of the pancreatic parenchyma were also evaluated. Predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.

42859212.label: Results
42859212.text: PPAP occurred in 41 patients. Four models were compared: a clinical-morphologic model (age and main pancreatic duct [MPD] dilation), a conventional model (age, MPD dilation and arterial-to-portal ratio [A/P]), a radiomics model (rad-score alone), and a radiomics-integrated model (age, MPD dilation and rad-score). The radiomics-integrated model achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) among the four models, with the AUC of 0.854 (95% CI 0.758-0.951) in the training set and 0.862 (95% CI 0.732-0.993) in the test set.

42859212.label: Conclusion
42859212.text: The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

42878962.label: Objectives
42878962.text: In the Netherlands, post-mortem radiology aids forensic investigation, using a full-body post-mortem computed tomography (PMCT) scan and a post-mortem magnetic resonance imaging (PMMRI) scan in specific cases. Application of PMMRI varies between countries and institutions in the absence of international guidelines. This study analyses current use and added value of PMMRI in a single forensic imaging institution in the Netherlands.

42878962.label: Materials and methods
42878962.text: All post-mortem cases scanned between July 2024 and July 2025 were included, except non-accidental injury protocol cases. The (contra-)indications for additional PMMRI scans in addition to PMCT were recorded. On the same day as image evaluation, added value was scored by the forensic radiologist and consultant using the following options: additional finding, exclusion of a finding, confirmation of PMCT and no added value.

42878962.label: Results
42878962.text: PMMRI was conducted in 47.4% of all cases, indicated by suspected strangulation, penetrating injuries, blunt force trauma and lesions seen on PMCT. In suspected strangulation, PMMRI neck showed additional findings or exclusion of findings in 31/46 cases, while PMMRI brain had the lowest added value in 13/25 cases. PMMRI thorax and abdomen showed additional findings in 14/20 and 4/9 cases of penetrating trauma, respectively. Additional findings were found in 10/15 PMMRI brain scans and 6/8 PMMRI thorax scans, based on PMCT.

42878962.label: Conclusion
42878962.text: Application of PMMRI in addition to PMCT is currently used in a targeted manner. In cases of strangulation and penetrating injuries, additional or excluded findings were found. Therefore, adding PMMRI in these specific cases can be of added value.

42878962.label: Key points
42878962.text: Question What is the added value of post-mortem MRI in forensic cases, in the absence of international guidelines and standardised indications? Findings Additional findings were observed in post-mortem MRI examinations indicated for soft tissue injuries caused by penetrating force and in cases of suspected strangulation. Critical Relevance Statement The criminal investigation can be optimised by using post-mortem MRI in addition to post-mortem CT, either by showing additional findings on post-mortem MRI not seen on CT, or by excluding findings with higher certainty.

43079112.label: Purpose
43079112.text: To evaluate "pseudoenhancement" in adnexal lesions on low kiloelectron volt (keV) virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) at photon-counting CT (PCCT) and to establish optimal attenuation change thresholds for distinguishing enhancing from nonenhancing lesions at each VMI.

43079112.label: Methods
43079112.text: Adult women who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic PCCT and pelvic MRI or ultrasound (US) within 180 days were identified via retrospective PACS search. Adnexal lesions were classified as enhancing or nonenhancing using MRI or US as the reference standard. Quantitative attenuation measurements were obtained using regions-of-interest at VMI levels (70, 67, 60, 55, 50, 45, and 40 keV). "Pseudoenhancement" was defined as ≥ 20 Hounsfield units (HU) increase between the VMI and virtual unenhanced (VUE) images. The diagnostic performance of a 20HU change to define enhancement at each VMI level was assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine optimal thresholds by maximizing the Youden index. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients.

43079112.label: Results
43079112.text: Forty-five women (median [IQR] age 46 years [37, 54] ) with 30 nonenhancing and 15 enhancing adnexal lesions were included. No "pseudoenhancement" was observed at 70 or 67 keV; however, "pseudoenhancement" was observed in 3.3% of patients at 60 keV, increasing to 26.7% at 40 keV. Using a 20 HU change to indicate enhancement had 47% sensitivity with 100% specificity at 70 keV and 93% sensitivity with 73% specificity at 40 keV. Optimal attenuation thresholds increased with decreasing energy, from 10.0 HU at 70 keV to 36.3 HU at 40 keV. Notably, at 60 keV, the threshold was 19.1HU. Inter-reader agreement was near perfect (ICC = 0.858, 95%CI = 0.756-0.920).

43079112.label: Conclusion
43079112.text: "Pseudoenhancement" of adnexal lesions occurs with increasing frequency with decreasing keV below 60 keV, but there was no "pseudoenhancement" at 67 or 70 keV. Energy-specific attenuation thresholds improve adnexal lesion characterization.
